titleZh: 数值、单位、变量与表达式
title:
数值、单位、变量与表达式

Numbers, units, variables, and expressions

blocks.text: 上一章把一个手算保存成了程序。本章进一步回答：程序中的数值代表什么，为什么同一个数字配上不同单位会成为不同的量，计算顺序如何确定，以及测量值为什么不能被当成绝对精确的真值。所有例子仍然只使用基础算术和已经见过的Python语法。

The previous chapter saved a hand calculation as a program. This chapter asks what a value represents, why the same number with a different unit becomes a different quantity, how evaluation order is determined, and why a measurement is not an exact truth. Every example still uses basic arithmetic and Python syntax already introduced.

blocks.caption: 单位尺度图的阅读任务：先确认对象和尺度，再进行换算。

blocks.text: 你将能把一个带单位的物理量写成可检查的表达式，并说明测量精度的边界。
You will write a unit-bearing physical quantity as a checkable expression and state the boundary of measurement precision.
2.1 数字与量不是一回事 2.1 A number is not a quantity

blocks.right: 数字 + 单位 + 对象
blocks.note: 在机器人中还常要补充方向、坐标系和时间。 / Robotics often also needs direction, frame, and time.

blocks.text: 数字 $7$ 只表示一个数值。$7$ mm、$7$ cm、$7$ s 和 $7$ kg 描述的是不同种类的量。量（quantity）至少包含数值和单位；在机器人系统中还经常需要对象、方向、坐标系和时间。现在先把最基本的数值与单位写清楚。

The number 7 is only a value. 7 mm, 7 cm, 7 s, and 7 kg describe different kinds of quantities. A quantity contains at least a value and a unit; robot systems often also require an object, direction, frame, and time. We begin by making values and units explicit.

blocks.title: 同一个7为什么不能直接相加 / Why two sevens may not be added

blocks.text: 叶片定位点偏差为 $7$ mm，机器人等待时间为 $7$ s。计算 $7+7=14$ 在算术上成立，但“$14$ mm-s”没有回答任何合理问题。加法要求两个量属于同一类对象并使用相容单位。

A blade datum has an error of 7 mm and the robot waits for 7 s. The arithmetic $7+7=14$ is valid, but “14 millimetre-seconds” answers no sensible question. Addition requires quantities of the same kind with compatible units.

blocks.title: 量纲与单位 / Dimension and unit

blocks.text: 量纲（dimension）描述量的类别，例如长度、时间和质量；单位（unit）给出测量这种量所使用的尺度，例如长度可以用m、cm或mm。$2$ m和$200$ cm数值不同，但表示相同长度；$2$ m和$2$ s数值相同，却不是同类量。

A dimension describes a kind of quantity, such as length, time, or mass. A unit gives the scale used to measure it, such as metres, centimetres, or millimetres for length. 2 m and 200 cm have different numerical values but the same length; 2 m and 2 s share a value but are different kinds of quantities.
2.2 单位换算是乘以一个等于1的比例 2.2 Unit conversion multiplies by a ratio equal to one
因为 $1\ \mathrm{m}=1000\ \mathrm{mm}$，比值 $1\ \mathrm{m}/1000\ \mathrm{mm}$ 表示同一长度除以自身，其大小等于1。将 $35$ mm换成m可以写成
Since $1\ \mathrm{m}=1000\ \mathrm{mm}$, the ratio $1\ \mathrm{m}/1000\ \mathrm{mm}$ divides one length by the same length and therefore equals one. Converting 35 mm to metres can be written as
分子和分母中的mm相消，留下m。这个写法比死记“除以1000”更可靠，因为方向错了会在单位上暴露。把 $0.035$ m换回mm时，应使用相反的比例。

Millimetres cancel between numerator and denominator, leaving metres. This is safer than memorising “divide by 1000,” because a reversed conversion becomes visible in the units. To convert 0.035 m back to millimetres, use the reciprocal ratio.

blocks.code:
offset_mm = 35
offset_m = offset_mm / 1000
recovered_mm = offset_m * 1000

assert offset_m == 0.035
assert recovered_mm == offset_mm
print(offset_m)

blocks.text: 往返检查（round-trip check）验证从A换到B再换回A是否恢复原值。它不能证明所有单位逻辑都正确，但能捕获许多换算方向和倍率错误。
A round-trip check converts from A to B and back to A, then checks whether the original value is recovered. It does not prove all unit logic, but catches many direction and scale errors.
2.3 整数与小数 2.3 Integers and decimal numbers
Python用不同类型表示不同种类的数据。`35` 是整数（integer），`0.035` 是浮点数（floating-point number）。浮点数用于表示带小数的近似实数。这里的“浮点”涉及计算机怎样存储小数，后面的数值计算章节会深入解释；现在只需要知道某些十进制小数不能被二进制计算机精确存储。

Python uses different types for different kinds of data. `35` is an integer and `0.035` is a floating-point number. Floating-point values approximate real numbers with decimals. Later numerical-computing chapters explain their representation; for now, know that some decimal fractions cannot be stored exactly in binary.
`abs` 计算绝对值。这里检查的不是两个浮点数完全相同，而是差异小于 $10^{-12}$。容差不能随意设得很大；它必须比任务允许的误差更严格，并与数值尺度相匹配。

`abs` computes absolute value. The check asks whether the difference is smaller than $10^{-12}$ rather than requiring exact equality. A tolerance must not be chosen arbitrarily large; it should be stricter than the task error allowance and appropriate to the scale.
2.4 表达式的执行顺序 2.4 Evaluation order in an expression
表达式 $2+3\times4$ 按照先乘除、后加减得到 $14$，而 $(2+3)\times4$ 得到 $20$。Python采用相同的基本优先级。即使你记得规则，在涉及单位换算、平均值或误差公式时也应使用括号明确结构。

The expression $2+3\times4$ evaluates multiplication first and gives 14, whereas $(2+3)\times4$ gives 20. Python uses the same basic precedence. Even when precedence is known, parentheses should expose the intended structure in unit conversions, averages, and error formulas.

blocks.title: 平均值中的括号 / Parentheses in an average

blocks.text: Three measurements are 10.1, 9.9, and 10.0 mm. Their mean is $(10.1+9.9+10.0)/3=10.0$ mm. Writing `10.1 + 9.9 + 10.0 / 3` divides only the final value by three and no longer computes the mean.

blocks.code:
measurement_1_mm = 10.1
measurement_2_mm = 9.9
measurement_3_mm = 10.0

mean_mm = (
    measurement_1_mm + measurement_2_mm + measurement_3_mm
) / 3
assert abs(mean_mm - 10.0) < 1e-12

blocks.text: 2.5 变量会随执行顺序改变 2.5 Variables change with execution order
数学中的等式 $x=x+1$ 不可能对普通实数成立，因为两边相减会得到 $0=1$。Python中的 `x = x + 1` 不是数学等式：它先读取旧值，计算加一，再把名字 `x` 关联到新值。

The mathematical equation $x=x+1$ cannot hold for an ordinary real number, because subtraction would give $0=1$. In Python, `x = x + 1` is not an equation: it reads the old value, adds one, and associates `x` with the new value.

blocks.code:
sample_count = 0
sample_count = sample_count + 1
sample_count = sample_count + 1
assert sample_count == 2

blocks.text: 这使程序能够记录状态，但也意味着不能脱离执行顺序阅读代码。以后循环会反复执行这种更新；机器人状态、训练步数和实验计数都依赖这一机制。

This allows a program to record state, but means code cannot be read without execution order. Loops later repeat such updates; robot state, training steps, and experiment counts all use this mechanism.
2.6 测量值不是绝对真值 2.6 A measurement is not an exact truth

blocks.note: 最后一位数字必须与仪器分辨率相称。 / The final digit must match instrument resolution.

blocks.text: 用最小刻度为 $1$ mm的直尺测量一个物体并读出 $35$ mm，不代表真实长度恰好是数学意义上的 $35.000\ldots$ mm。读数受刻度分辨率、视角、放置方式和操作者影响。测量记录至少应包含数值、单位和测量条件。

Reading 35 mm from a ruler with 1 mm divisions does not imply that the true length is exactly $35.000\ldots$ mm. The reading depends on resolution, viewing angle, placement, and operator. A measurement record should contain at least a value, unit, and measurement condition.

blocks.title: 误差、不确定性与容差先做区分 / First distinction among error, uncertainty, and tolerance

blocks.text: 误差（error）通常指测量或估计与参考值之间的差；不确定性（uncertainty）描述我们对值缺乏确定性的程度；容差（tolerance）是任务允许的偏差范围。三者相关但不相同。本章只建立区别，概率与统计章节再给出正式方法。

Error commonly means the difference between a measurement or estimate and a reference. Uncertainty describes limited knowledge of a value. Tolerance is the deviation allowed by a task. They are related but not identical. This chapter establishes the distinction; probability and statistics chapters provide formal methods.
如果叶片装配允许的位置误差为 $0.02$ mm，而测量工具只能稳定分辨 $1$ mm，那么增加小数位不会解决问题。`35.000000` 看起来更精确，但没有增加测量信息。

If blade assembly allows 0.02 mm of position error while the measuring tool reliably resolves only 1 mm, adding decimal places does not solve the problem. `35.000000` looks more precise but contains no additional measurement information.
2.7 一份最小测量程序 2.7 A minimal measurement program

blocks.caption: 单位、平均值和容差的最小实验 / Minimal experiment with units, mean, and tolerance
blocks.code:
"""Minimal measurement experiment for Chapter 2."""

measurement_1_mm = 10.1
measurement_2_mm = 9.9
measurement_3_mm = 10.0

mean_mm = (
    measurement_1_mm + measurement_2_mm + measurement_3_mm
) / 3

target_mm = 10.0
tolerance_mm = 0.2
absolute_error_mm = abs(mean_mm - target_mm)
within_tolerance = absolute_error_mm <= tolerance_mm

assert abs(mean_mm - 10.0) < 1e-12
assert absolute_error_mm < 1e-12
assert within_tolerance

print(mean_mm)
print(absolute_error_mm)
print(within_tolerance)

blocks.text: 程序保留三次读数的单位，计算平均值，再比较平均值与目标值的绝对差。最后的布尔值 `within_tolerance` 只有真（`True`）或假（`False`）两种结果；下一章会正式解释比较和布尔值。现在先预测三个打印结果，再运行并与预测比较。

The program preserves the unit of three readings, computes their mean, and compares the absolute difference from a target. The Boolean value `within_tolerance` is either `True` or `False`; the next chapter formally introduces comparisons and Booleans. For now, predict the three printed results and compare them with the run.

blocks.title: 单位一致，测量仍可能无效 / Compatible units do not guarantee a valid measurement

blocks.text: 三次读数可能都来自同一把未校准直尺，因此平均值非常稳定却整体偏移。重复测量可以观察随机波动，但不能自动消除系统偏差。后续统计章节会把随机误差和系统误差分开。

All three readings may come from the same uncalibrated ruler, producing a stable mean with a common offset. Repetition reveals random variation but does not automatically remove systematic bias. Later statistics chapters separate random and systematic error.
2.8 多场景连接 2.8 Connections across robot scenarios

间隙、力和力矩阈值失去意义

blocks.text: 这些案例只建立“数值必须带语义”的共同原则，不要求现在理解导航、力矩或神经网络。等相应概念正式出现时，我们会回到同一张表并增加数学和代码。

These cases establish only the shared principle that a value needs semantics. Navigation, torque, and neural networks are not prerequisites here. When each topic is introduced, we return to the same table with additional mathematics and code.
2.9 练习、答案与完成标准 2.9 Exercises, answers, and completion standard

items: 把 $250$ mm换成m，再换回mm；写出单位相消过程和Python断言。
计算 $(2+6)/4$ 与 $2+6/4$，解释括号改变了哪一步。
预测连续执行三次 `count = count + 2` 后的值，其中初值为1。
给出一个“数值相同但量纲不同”和一个“数值不同但表示同一量”的例子。
三次测量都为 $10.8$ mm，目标是 $10.0$ mm。说明“没有波动”为什么不代表“没有误差”。
将2.7节中的容差从 $0.2$ mm改为 $0.05$ mm，先预测布尔结果，再运行。

blocks.text: 第1题为 $0.25$ m，往返应恢复 $250$ mm。第2题分别为2和3.5。第3题为7。第4题可用 $7$ m与 $7$ s，以及 $1$ m与 $100$ cm。第5题说明重复值只能表示当前读数一致，与参考值仍相差 $0.8$ mm。第6题必须使用程序实际计算出的平均值与目标差进行判断，不能只凭肉眼看读数。

Exercise 1 gives 0.25 m and the round trip restores 250 mm. Exercise 2 gives 2 and 3.5. Exercise 3 gives 7. Exercise 4 may use 7 m versus 7 s, and 1 m versus 100 cm. In Exercise 5, repeated readings agree with one another but remain 0.8 mm from the reference. Exercise 6 must compare the computed mean-target difference rather than judge by sight.
不用看书，解释数值、量、量纲、单位、变量、表达式、误差、不确定性和容差的区别。然后运行2.7节程序，改变一个读数并预测哪些输出会改变。
保存一次包含原始读数、单位、平均值、目标、容差、预测和实际结果的运行记录。下一章将正式建立相等、大小比较、方程、不等式和布尔判断。
